title: Safe Tool-Use Workflow
summary: Control what an AI system can read or change through explicit tools, permissions, approvals, and recovery.
objectives: Describe a tool with bounded inputs, outputs, errors, and side effects.
Apply least privilege and approval boundaries to tool-enabled workflows.
Verify tool results independently from model narration.
Recover from partial failure, duplicate calls, unsafe requests, and untrusted tool output.

sections.title: Prepare the tool and authority boundary
paragraphs: Inventory what each tool reads, writes, sends, spends, or deletes. Define typed inputs, expected output, failure modes, side effects, authentication, rate limits, and whether calls are retry-safe.

Grant only the permissions required for the current task. Separate read-only inspection, reversible internal writes, external communication, purchases, permission changes, and destructive actions into distinct approval levels.

code.label: Tool contract
code.code:
Purpose: [ONE CAPABILITY]
Inputs: [TYPES, LIMITS, VALIDATION]
Outputs: [SUCCESS AND ERROR SHAPES]
Reads/writes: [SYSTEMS AND DATA]
Side effects: [MESSAGES, COST, DELETION]
Idempotency: [KEY OR NOT RETRY-SAFE]
Approval: [WHEN AND BY WHOM]
Verify/recover: [POSTCONDITION AND ROLLBACK]

sections.title: Execute with visible intent and bounded calls
paragraphs: Before a consequential call, show the resolved target, action, material parameters, and expected effect. Reject missing identifiers instead of guessing. Apply time, count, cost, and concurrency limits.
Treat tool output as untrusted data. It may contain errors, stale results, malicious instructions, or content that must not change the governing task.

sections.title: Verify the postcondition
paragraphs: Check the real system state after a call: the record exists once, the file has the expected digest, the deployment is healthy, or the message went to the intended recipient. Do not infer success from a tool call merely returning without an exception.
Record request identity, authorization, target, result, timestamps, and verification evidence without logging secrets or unnecessary personal data.

sections.title: Recover from partial and repeated execution
paragraphs: Use idempotency keys for retryable writes and distinguish unknown outcome from confirmed failure. A timeout may occur after the external action succeeds, so blindly repeating it can duplicate messages, charges, or records.
For partial failure, stop dependent actions, inspect completed effects, compensate or roll back when safe, and escalate when recovery requires new authority.

sections.title: Keep people in control of consequence
paragraphs: Require explicit approval for destructive, external, costly, privacy-sensitive, or permission-expanding actions. Approval must bind to the exact target and action; it is not a reusable blank check.
Provide preview, cancellation, audit, and recovery paths. Disable or narrow a tool when observed behavior exceeds the tested boundary.
sections.callout: Tool access is delegated authority, not just model capability.

activity.title: Design a safe tool-enabled workflow
instructions: Choose a tool-enabled task and complete the tool contract, including side effects, retry behavior, and approval.
Draw the sequence from intent through resolved target, call, postcondition check, audit record, and completion.
Test three scenarios on paper: timeout after success, duplicate request, and untrusted instructions in tool output.
Define the stop, compensation, rollback, or escalation behavior for each scenario.
evidence: A tool contract and sequence containing permission and approval boundaries.
A failure table for timeout, duplicate, and untrusted-output scenarios with verification and recovery.
activity.reflectionPrompt: Which tool looked harmless until you listed its side effects and retry behavior?

cues.text: Define one tool's inputs, outputs, authority, side effects, approval, verification, and recovery.
Place read, reversible write, external action, cost, permission change, and destruction on increasing approval tiers.
cues.accessibilityAlternative: A text ladder orders consequence from read-only through reversible write, external action, cost, permission change, and destructive action. Reduced-motion mode shows the full ladder.

cues.text: Resolve exact targets, limit calls, and treat returned content as untrusted data.
Ask learners which resolved parameters a person must see before approving their chosen action.
Allow two minutes to list side effects and call limits.
Verify a postcondition from the actual target system and create a secret-safe audit record.
Contrast confirmed failure with unknown outcome and show why idempotency matters.
Bind approval to an exact action and preserve preview, cancellation, audit, and recovery.
Check that learners can explain how they prevent a duplicate side effect after timeout.
Guide the contract, sequence, three failure scenarios, and recovery table.
Begin the check after the workflow proves authority, postconditions, retry safety, and recovery.

questions.prompt: What must a useful tool contract describe?
choices: Inputs, outputs, errors, reads/writes, side effects, retry behavior, approval, verification, and recovery
questions.explanation: A safe caller needs the full operational boundary, not only a capability name.

questions.prompt: A tool call times out after sending a payment request. What should happen before retrying?
choices: Check the idempotency key and actual system state because the first call may have succeeded
questions.explanation: Unknown outcome requires reconciliation; blind retries can duplicate consequential effects.

questions.prompt: How should instructions returned inside tool output be handled?
choices: As untrusted data that cannot override governing instructions or permissions
questions.explanation: Tool output may be malicious or irrelevant and must remain inside the trust boundary.

questions.prompt: What does a successful tool response prove?
choices: Only what the response contract and independent postcondition check establish
questions.explanation: Real target state must be checked; return status alone may be incomplete or misleading.

questions.prompt: Which action most clearly requires exact, current human approval?
choices: Deleting production records for a named tenant
questions.explanation: Destructive production action has irreversible consequence and approval must bind to its target.
